overview: Alimentation Couche-Tard is a Canadian (Laval, Québec-headquartered) global convenience store and road transportation fuel retailer, operating primarily under the Circle K banner (plus Couche-Tard in Québec and Ingo for automated fuel in Europe). As of fiscal year-end April 26, 2026, the network comprised close to 17,300 stores worldwide -- 9,356 company/affiliate stores in North America, 4,820 in Europe, 387 company-operated in Hong Kong, and more than 2,700 licensed Circle K stores across 12 other countries. The company reports in US dollars under IFRS and trades on the TSX under ATD, with a market capitalization of roughly CAD $70 billion.

business_model.summary: Couche-Tard earns revenue from three categories: road transportation fuel (retail and wholesale), in-store merchandise and services (nicotine, beverages, beer/wine/liquor, food service, other), and other (stationary/aviation fuel, rental income). Fuel is the larger revenue driver (73% of fiscal 2026 revenue, $56.2B) but merchandise carries far higher margins, so the two categories contribute roughly evenly to gross profit (fuel 50% / merchandise 48% / other 2% of fiscal 2026 gross profit of $14.46B). Within merchandise, nicotine products are the single largest category (38.6% of merchandise sales), followed by beverages (17.8%), other (18.5%), beer/wine/liquor (11.9%) and food service (13.2%, a strategic growth priority). Revenue is largely transactional/high-frequency (daily convenience purchases, fuel fill-ups) rather than subscription-based, though loyalty program (Inner Circle) engagement and franchise/license royalty streams add a modest recurring component. Growth is a mix of organic same-store sales/traffic and an active M&A roll-up strategy consolidating a fragmented convenience industry.
business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market convenience/fuel consumers, with a B2B wholesale fuel and merchandise distribution business to independent operators, franchisees and dealers
business_model.geographic_mix: Fiscal 2026 revenue: United States ~57% ($43.7B), Europe and other regions ~33% ($25.1B), Canada ~10% ($7.7B). Gross profit mix skews more to the US (64%) given richer US merchandise margins, with Europe and other at 26% and Canada at 10%.

main_competitors: integrated oil company-branded convenience chains (Shell, etc.)
competitive_position.market_position: Ranked No. 2 in the 2026 U.S. Convenience Store News Top 100 (behind 7-Eleven, ahead of Casey's). Circle K held roughly 4.98% of US fuel-site market share in 2025 versus Shell's ~8.2% (per NACS-sourced data), underscoring that even the largest players operate in a highly fragmented ~150,000-store US market. Couche-Tard describes itself as the leader in Canadian convenience retail, one of the largest independent US convenience operators, a leader in Scandinavian/Baltic/Belgian/Irish convenience and mobility retail, and holder of an 'enviable' position in Hong Kong.

moat_factors.description: ~17,300 stores and ~$77B revenue generate procurement leverage with fuel suppliers and CPG vendors, supporting a fuel break-even the company claims is well below the industry average and ongoing cost synergies from acquisitions (e.g., TotalEnergies European assets, targeting €170M run-rate synergies by FY2029).
Owns ~5,900 lots and ~7,300 buildings, giving flexibility and reducing rent exposure versus pure operators; dense multi-market footprint diversifies local demand/fuel-price shocks.

moat_factors.factor: Integrated fuel supply chain / fuel terminals
moat_factors.description: Owned fuel terminals (including recent German acquisitions) and wholesale fuel operations let Couche-Tard capture margin volatility upside, as seen in the strong Q4 FY2026 fuel margins driven by commodity volatility.
Extensive portfolio of control brands (Circle K, Simply Great, Meadowbrook, Arizona iced tea license, etc.) differentiates assortment and supports margin versus pure fuel-only competitors.

Decades of successful roll-up acquisitions since 1997 (Statoil, The Pantry, CST Brands/Circle K, Holiday, TotalEnergies Europe, GetGo) with a repeatable playbook for synergy capture; now pursuing its largest-ever deal (Żabka Group).
Entrepreneurial, store-as-profit-center culture and a globally consolidated Circle K brand (since FY2020) build consistency and local agility simultaneously.

weaknesses: Thin, commoditized core fuel business with volatile margins subject to wholesale price swings and regulatory constraints in some jurisdictions
Secular decline in cigarette/tobacco volumes (largest single merchandise category at ~39% of merchandise sales) pressures same-store merchandise growth, particularly in Canada
Heavy reliance on US market (57% of revenue) exposes the company to US consumer discretionary softness, especially among lower-income customers

Antitrust scrutiny limits the pace/size of further large-scale US consolidation (FTC-mandated divestitures in GetGo and prior Holiday deals; a $3.5M FTC civil penalty for violating a prior divestiture order)
Long tail of smaller, nimble regional operators (QuikTrip, Wawa, Kwik Trip) often out-execute on fresh food and customer experience in their home markets

growth_drivers: 'Core + More' strategy (announced February 11, 2026): amplify core traffic drivers (fuel, nicotine, thirst) while investing in food service, private label, car wash, mobility and network expansion

Active M&A roll-up of a fragmented convenience industry: GetGo acquisition closed June 2025 (270 sites, $1.6B) and the pending ~$8.6B acquisition of Poland's Żabka Group (announced July 31, 2026) -- Couche-Tard's largest deal ever, pending EU/Polish antitrust clearance
Continued integration synergies from the TotalEnergies European retail asset acquisition (targeting ~€170M annual run-rate synergies by fiscal 2029, ~€61M already realized ~2 years post-close)
Fresh Food, Fast program and expanded food service / quick-service restaurant offerings to lift merchandise margins
Inner Circle loyalty program and digital/data analytics investments to drive traffic, basket size and personalized promotions
New US distribution center build-out (three new self-distribution centers opened in fiscal 2026: Otsego MN, Lockbourne OH, St. Louis MO) to improve supply chain efficiency
Disciplined capital return: renewed share buyback program (up to 77.1 million shares, ~10% of public float) and a 10.5% dividend increase for fiscal 2026
Store construction pipeline (103 new builds completed in FY2026, 34 more under construction) and selective market entry/expansion in Latin America and Southeast Asia
EV charging and mobility solutions as a longer-horizon adjacency to road fuel retail

business.description: Road transportation fuel gross margins swing materially quarter to quarter with commodity markets and are increasingly pressured by softer demand from higher retail prices; same-store fuel volumes declined in the US and Europe in fiscal 2026 even as margins improved.
Nicotine products are ~39% of merchandise sales; cigarette volumes are in secular decline industry-wide, requiring offsetting growth in other nicotine, beverages and food service.
The pending ~$8.6B Żabka Group acquisition (Couche-Tard's largest ever) and ongoing TotalEnergies integration carry execution risk on synergy capture and cross-border operating model fit.

business.risk: Customer/traffic sensitivity to low-income consumer stress
business.description: FY2025 same-store merchandise softness was explicitly tied to constrained discretionary spending among lower-income US/Canadian consumers.

financial.risk: Rising debt load and interest expense from acquisitions
financial.description: Total debt has grown from ~$9.6B (FY2021) to ~$16.4B (FY2026) alongside acquisitions (TotalEnergies, GetGo) and multiple note issuances (CAD, USD, EUR tranches in FY2026); leverage ratio stood at 1.99x at FY2026 year-end, still investment-grade but rising with the pending Żabka deal, which is expected to be financed with new debt facilities.

Reports in USD but earns in CAD, EUR, NOK, SEK, DKK, PLN and HKD; FX translation swung reported revenue and expenses by hundreds of millions of dollars in recent quarters, and the company uses cross-currency swaps (e.g., converting CAD notes to EUR) to manage exposure.
Effective tax rate moved from 20.8% (FY2024) to 22.0% (FY2025) to 23.7% in Q4 FY2026 due to earnings-mix shifts across jurisdictions.

regulatory.description: History of FTC-mandated divestitures (Holiday, GetGo/Giant Eagle -- 35 sites divested in FY2026) and a prior $3.5M FTC penalty for violating an earlier consent order; the collapsed Seven & I bid was explicitly derailed in part by anticipated antitrust hurdles given store overlap; future large US deals will face similar scrutiny.
The pending Żabka Group tender offer requires European Commission or Polish competition authority merger clearance before closing.

Tobacco, alcohol, lottery, cannabis/CBD and nicotine products are subject to evolving, jurisdiction-specific regulation; fuel, milk and alcohol pricing are subject to price regulation in some markets.
Ongoing remediation liability exposure for current/former contaminated fuel sites and evolving environmental/biofuel-blending standards, particularly in the EU.

macro.risk: EV transition / long-term fuel demand erosion
macro.description: Vehicle electrification could structurally reduce road transportation fuel volumes over the medium-to-long term, though offset partially by rising per-gallon margins and industry consolidation; pace varies sharply by geography.
Convenience/fuel demand is sensitive to macro consumer strength, fuel prices and employment/commuting patterns; recent softness was concentrated among lower-income consumers.
Net financial expenses have risen with higher average debt balances; a growing acquisition-funded debt stack increases sensitivity to rate levels on refinancing.
Wholesale fuel costs, and to a lesser extent food/beverage input costs, flow through cost of sales and can compress merchandise and fuel gross margins in volatile commodity environments.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global convenience/fuel retail industry remains large and fragmented (>150,000 US sites alone), supporting continued consolidation. Management's own long-term framework (Core + More, Feb 2026) targets mid-single-digit merchandise/service revenue growth, inflation-linked fuel gross profit growth, and high-single-digit EBITDA growth through fiscal 2030 -- implying a maturing but still-consolidating industry rather than a high-growth one.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Fuel volumes track macro driving activity and consumer fuel-price sensitivity; merchandise sales (especially discretionary/food service) are sensitive to consumer spending power, while nicotine/beverage 'core' categories are relatively defensive.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- rising acquisition-funded debt load (leverage ratio 1.99x at FY2026 year-end, set to rise further with the debt-financed Żabka deal) increases sensitivity to interest rates on refinancing and new issuance.
key_input_costs: Electronic payment processing fees (a meaningful and growing opex line tied to fuel transaction volume)

recent_developments.event: Closed acquisition of 270 GetGo Café + Market sites from Giant Eagle for $1.6 billion; later agreed to FTC-mandated divestiture of 35 sites in Pennsylvania/Indiana/Ohio to secure regulatory approval.

Formally withdrew its roughly $46-47 billion takeover proposal for Seven & I Holdings (parent of 7-Eleven) after about a year of negotiations, citing lack of constructive engagement from the target; Couche-Tard shares rose as much as ~18.5% on the news while Seven & I shares fell ~9%.

Issued a series of senior unsecured notes across currencies (CAD $500M due 2032, USD $700M due 2028 and $500M due 2035, EUR €750M due 2033) to refinance maturing debt and fund general corporate purposes/acquisitions; used cross-currency swaps to manage currency mix of debt.
Held its 2026 Business Strategy Update, introducing the 'Core + More' framework and new long-term financial guidance (through fiscal 2030) that superseded all prior outlooks.

Reported fiscal 2026 results (year ended April 26, 2026): revenue $76.5B (+5.0%), adjusted EBITDA $7.0B, net earnings attributable to shareholders $3.14B (diluted EPS $3.37), including a $260.9M net legal recovery from payment card interchange fee litigation; declared a 10.5% dividend increase to CA $0.84/share annually and repurchased 30 million shares (~8.7% more than FY2025) for $1.6 billion under its renewed buyback program.

Announced a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling stake in Żabka Group (Poland's largest convenience retailer) via a voluntary tender offer at PLN 32/share, valuing equity at roughly US$8.6 billion -- Couche-Tard's largest acquisition ever; backed by irrevocable tender commitments from CVC Capital Partners, Partners Group and Żabka management (~57% of shares), financed via fully committed debt facilities; subject to EU/Polish antitrust clearance, with intent to squeeze out minority holders and delist from Warsaw if 95% ownership is reached.

Reported Q1 fiscal 2027 results (quarter ended July 19, 2026): revenue $21.7B (+25.1% YoY, largely acquisition- and fuel-price-driven), adjusted EBITDA +10.5%, adjusted diluted EPS +15.4% to approximately $0.90; US merchandise margin compressed ~50bps to 34.1% and Canadian same-store sales were roughly flat amid continued tobacco category softness.

guidance.as_of: 2026 Business Strategy Update (February 11, 2026), reaffirmed in FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 results

items.notes: Part of the Core + More long-term framework

items.metric: Total merchandise and service revenue growth
items.notes: Includes contribution from bolt-on M&A and network expansion, not just organic same-store growth

items.metric: Road transportation fuel gross profit growth
items.notes: Reflects a maturing, margin- rather than volume-driven fuel growth outlook given EV transition headwinds

items.target: in line with inflation or lower
items.notes: Cost discipline target; normalized expense growth was 3.1% in FY2026 (vs. 3.4% in FY2025)
Underpinned by Fit-to-Serve cost program targeted to contribute ~$850 million of EBITDA by FY2030
Benefits from EBITDA growth plus continued share buybacks; excludes the impact of any transformative M&A such as Żabka
Actual FY2026 free cash flow of ~$3.37 billion (per Metrics.csv) exceeded this target

guidance.management_commentary: Management explicitly stated the long-term guidance 'does not take into account the completion of any transactions that would significantly alter our portfolio, business segments, or strategic direction' -- meaning the pending Żabka Group acquisition and any future large M&A sit outside the base guidance. CFO commentary following Q3 FY2026 results described results as 'validating the actions outlined in our Business Strategy Update.' Management has emphasized disciplined, return-focused capital allocation (noting it will not overpay or chase growth for its own sake) following the collapse of its Seven & I pursuit, while continuing to pursue bolt-on and larger strategic acquisitions (GetGo, Żabka) that meet its financial return criteria.

bull_case: Proven, repeatable M&A roll-up playbook in a still-highly-fragmented global convenience industry, now extending into new geographies (Poland via Żabka) with a credible long-term synergy capture record (TotalEnergies integration on track)

New long-term guidance (Core + More) targets double-digit adjusted EPS growth through FY2030, combining mid-single-digit EBITDA growth with continued aggressive share buybacks (renewed program covering up to 10% of public float)
Resolution of the Seven & I distraction removes execution/antitrust overhang and refocuses capital allocation on disciplined, return-criteria-based deals, reducing binary mega-deal risk to the thesis

Structurally improving fuel economics -- industry consolidation has driven a multi-year rise in per-gallon fuel margins even as volumes soften, and Couche-Tard's integrated supply chain/terminals let it capture volatility upside

Investment-grade balance sheet (leverage ratio ~2.0x) with strong, growing free cash flow (>$2.5B FY2026 target, actual higher) provides flexibility to fund growth capex, buybacks, a rising dividend (+10.5% in FY2026) and further M&A simultaneously
bear_case: Long-term EV adoption could structurally erode road transportation fuel volumes, the largest single revenue category (73% of FY2026 revenue), pressuring a business built around high-frequency fuel-driven store visits

Antitrust risk remains a persistent constraint on further large-scale US consolidation, as shown by repeated FTC-mandated divestitures (GetGo, Holiday) and a prior penalty for violating a consent order -- limiting the most capital-efficient growth lever in its largest market

Rising debt load from successive acquisitions (total debt roughly $9.6B in FY2021 to $16.4B in FY2026, set to increase further with the debt-financed ~$8.6B Żabka deal) increases financial and interest-rate risk if fuel margins or consumer spending soften simultaneously

Secular decline in cigarettes/tobacco (largest merchandise category at ~39% of merchandise sales) is a structural headwind to same-store merchandise growth that must be offset by newer, less-proven categories (food service, other nicotine, private label)

Integration risk and cross-border execution complexity on the largest acquisition in company history (Żabka, a different market structure/franchise model in Poland) following a recent string of acquisitions (GetGo, TotalEnergies Europe) still being digested
